items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: So, I missed Mozart, but I did get to be a W.C. Handy, so.

ctx.x: That was the name of the piece. Well, I went up there, and she actually took it down and then made a piano copy. Well, with a piano out or anything, now, this was something, really something new in my life, see. I didn't know anybody could do anything without the instrument. See, so when she did this, and I said, "What was that?", and she said it was a solfeggio. Well, I knew just as much then as I knew before, 'cause she could have said, "Spaghetti" it'd have been all the same to me. Solfeggio. Anyhow, so I was…

this was all about. And we copyrighted the piece. And my father and this woman laughed about it and they said, 'Well, your son is going to be a Mozart one day.' See. So, I missed Mozart, but I did get to be a W.C. Handy, so.
